facts.title: Antarctica Is the World's Largest Desert
facts.summary: Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth.

facts.title: Earth Has Gone Through Five Major Mass Extinctions
facts.summary: Scientists recognize five major mass extinctions in Earth's history, known as the Big Five: short spans when species died out far faster than new ones appeared.

facts.title: About 25 Tons of Space Dust Hit Earth's Atmosphere Every Day
facts.summary: Earth's atmosphere collects roughly 25 tons of cosmic dust every day, according to NASA.

facts.title: Earth's Gravity Is Slightly Stronger in Some Places Than Others
facts.summary: Gravity is not exactly the same everywhere on Earth.

facts.title: Earth's Inner Core Is About as Hot as the Surface of the Sun
facts.summary: The surface of Earth's solid inner core is estimated at about 5,700 K, or roughly 5,400 °C (9,800 °F), close to the temperature of the visible surface of the Sun.

facts.title: Earth's Inner Core May Have Paused Its Extra Spin Around 2009
facts.summary: Earth's solid inner core may turn at a slightly different rate from the rest of the planet, and a 2023 study suggests that this extra spin paused around 2009 and may now be reversing relative to the surface.

facts.title: A Fungus in Oregon May Be the Largest Living Organism on Earth
facts.summary: A single honey fungus, Armillaria ostoyae, growing in Oregon's Malheur National Forest, is considered one of the largest living organisms on Earth, if not the largest.

facts.title: Pando, a Single Aspen Clone in Utah, Is Thought to Be 9,000 to 16,000 Years Old
facts.summary: Pando, a single quaking aspen clone in Utah's Fishlake National Forest, is conservatively estimated to be 9,000 to 16,000 years old.

facts.title: Chile's 1960 Earthquake, the Strongest Ever Recorded, Shook for About 10 Minutes
facts.summary: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake in southern Chile, the most powerful ever recorded, shook the ground for about 10 minutes.

facts.title: The Ocean Produces About Half of Earth's Oxygen
facts.summary: Roughly half of the oxygen produced on Earth comes from the ocean, mostly from plankton: drifting plants, algae and some photosynthetic bacteria too small to see with the naked eye.

facts.title: The Ocean Makes Up About 99% of the Living Space on Earth
facts.summary: Measured by volume, the ocean makes up about 99% of the living space on Earth, according to the United Nations.

facts.title: Sunlight Takes About 8 Minutes and 19 Seconds to Reach Earth
facts.summary: Light leaving the Sun takes about 499 seconds, slightly more than 8 minutes and 19 seconds, to cross the average distance to Earth.

facts.title: The Deepest Point in the Ocean Is Deeper Than Mount Everest Is Tall
facts.summary: The Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific, is about 10,935 meters (35,876 feet) deep, the deepest known point in the ocean.

facts.title: The Fastest Wind Gust Ever Measured Outside a Tornado Hit 253 MPH
facts.summary: The fastest wind gust ever recorded outside a tornado reached 408 km/h (253 mph) on Barrow Island, off the coast of Western Australia, on 10 April 1996, during Tropical Cyclone Olivia.

facts.title: The Pacific Ring of Fire Holds About 75% of Earth's Volcanoes
facts.summary: About 75% of Earth's volcanoes, more than 450 of them, lie along the Ring of Fire, a horseshoe-shaped belt around the edges of the Pacific Ocean.

facts.title: The Tallest Waterfall on Earth Is Hidden Beneath the Ocean
facts.summary: The world's largest known waterfall is underwater, beneath the Denmark Strait between Greenland and Iceland.
